name: Garlic Butter Steak with Roasted Asparagus
pitch: A classic, satisfying combo that feels like a restaurant dinner but comes together in under 30 minutes with almost no effort.
steps: Preheat your oven to 425°F. Toss asparagus with oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet and roast for 12–15 minutes until tender and slightly crispy at the tips.
While the asparagus roasts, pat your steak dry, season generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Heat a skillet over high heat with a little oil. Sear the steak 3–4 minutes per side (for medium), then drop in a knob of butter and a smashed garlic clove and baste the steak for 1 minute.
Let the steak rest for 5 minutes before slicing, then plate everything up together — simple and delicious.

name: Steak and Asparagus Stir-Fry
pitch: Slice the steak thin and toss it with asparagus in a savory garlic-soy sauce — it's a quick, punchy weeknight dinner with an Asian-inspired twist.
steps: Slice the steak thinly against the grain and toss with a little soy sauce, a pinch of pepper, and a splash of oil. Let it sit while you prep the asparagus.
Trim and cut the asparagus into 2-inch pieces. Mix together 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp vinegar, and a pinch of pepper in a small bowl for your sauce.
Heat a wok or large skillet over high heat until very hot. Add oil, then stir-fry the steak in a single layer for 1–2 minutes until browned. Remove and set aside.

In the same pan, stir-fry the asparagus with garlic for 3–4 minutes, then return the steak, pour over the sauce, toss everything together, and serve — ideally over rice, though it's great on its own too.

name: Steak and Asparagus Frittata
pitch: This is a clever, hearty way to stretch your steak into a filling egg-based dinner that works any time of day — simple but satisfying.
steps: Preheat your broiler. Sear or pan-cook the steak to your liking, then let it rest and slice into small bite-sized pieces.
Blanch or lightly sauté the asparagus in an oven-safe skillet until just tender, about 3–4 minutes. Remove and cut into 1-inch pieces.
Whisk together 5–6 eggs with salt, pepper, and a little garlic powder. Pour the egg mixture into the skillet over medium heat, then scatter the steak and asparagus on top.
Cook undisturbed until the edges are set (about 4–5 minutes), then transfer the skillet to the broiler for 2–3 minutes until the top is golden and puffed. Slice like a pizza and serve.
